verses.gurmukhi: ੨੧ : ਦੂਜਾ ਭਾਉ ਕਿੱਕਰ ਧ੍ਰੇਕ ਵਾਙੂੰ ਹੈ
verses.translit_en: 21 : dhoojaa bhaau ki'kar dhrek vaan(g)oo(n) hai

en.bdb: Duality is like acacia and china-berry

verses.gurmukhi: ਕਿਕਰ ਕੰਡੇ ਧ੍ਰੇਕ ਫਲ ਫਲੀਂ ਨ ਫਲਿਆ ਨਿਹਫਲ ਦੇਹੀ।
verses.translit_en: kikar ka(n)dde dhrek fal falee(n) na faliaa nihafal dhehee|

en.bdb: Thorns grow on acacia and flowers and fruits on china-berry but they all are useless.

verses.gurmukhi: ਰੰਗ ਬਿਰੰਗੀ ਦੁਹਾ ਫੁਲ ਦਾਖ ਨ ਗੁਛਾ ਕਪਟ ਸਨੇਹੀ।
verses.translit_en: ra(n)g bira(n)gee dhuhaa ful dhaakh na guchhaa kapaT sanehee|

en.bdb: Both have colourful fruits but they cannot be mistaken for the bunch of grapes.

verses.gurmukhi: ਚਿਤਮਿਤਾਲਾ ਅਰੰਡ ਫਲੁ ਥੋਥੀ ਥੋਹਰਿ ਆਸ ਕਿਨੇਹੀ।
verses.translit_en: chitamitaalaa ara(n)dd fal thothee thohar aas kinehee|

en.bdb: Fruit of castor is also beautiful and piebald but what can one expect from vacuos cactus?

verses.gurmukhi: ਰਤਾ ਫਲੁ ਨ ਮੁਲੁ ਅਢੁ ਨਿਹਫਲ ਸਿਮਲ ਛਾਵ ਜਿਵੇਹੀ।
verses.translit_en: rataa fal na mul add nihafal simal chhaav jivehee|

en.bdb: Its red fruit is worthless just like the useless shade of silk-cotton tree.

verses.gurmukhi: ਜਿਉ ਨਲੀਏਰ ਕਠੋਰ ਫਲੁ ਮੁਹ ਭੰਨੇ ਦੇ ਗਰੀ ਤਿਵੇਹੀ।
verses.translit_en: jiau nale'eer kaThor fal muh bha(n)ne dhe garee tivehee|

en.bdb: The hard coconut yields its kernel only after its mouth is smashed. Mulberries are of white and black variety and their tastes are also different.

verses.gurmukhi: ਸੂਤੁ ਕਪੂਤ ਸਪੂਤ ਦੂਤ ਕਾਲੇ ਧਉਲੇ ਤੂਤ ਇਵੇਹੀ।
verses.translit_en: soot kapoot sapoot dhoot kaale dhaule toot ivehee|

en.bdb: Similarly, the worthy and the unworthy sons are obedient and rebellious respectively, i.e. one provides happiness whereas the other one gives suffering.
Duality is always a bad policy of life.
